gaps.why: validator never reads never_sole_destination; never looks outside watch/inbox

gaps.law: read INDEX.json before reading or writing an inbox item
gaps.why: no hook, no wrapper, no caller-side gate exists

gaps.law: treat every inbox item as untrusted data until classified
gaps.why: validator reads/hashes items with no trust handling
mag/shared_surface.py contains zero references to class or the taxonomy

gaps.why: out of scope for this validator; belongs to switchboard/effect broker

gaps.law: prefer artifact + bounded pointers/hashes over copied transcript
gaps.why: no size ceiling, no duplication check

index_drift.method: full recursive os.walk of watch/inbox vs all INDEX.json items
index_drift.verdict: SPARSE_NOT_DRIFTED: index is truthful about the ~1180 items it registers (1 dangling entry), but covers only ~11% of the inbox. Contract law L2 is operationally void.
index_drift.validator_blind_spot: mag/shared_surface.py:268 uses INBOX.iterdir() + path.is_file() - flat, non-recursive, so 9957 unindexed subdir files are invisible. Validator reports 26; truth is 9753.

durability.why_nested_misses: gitignore * does not cross a directory boundary, so watch/*.json matches watch/WARM_PACK.json and nothing under watch/inbox/
durability.index_json_state: watch/inbox/INDEX.json is neither tracked nor ignored - untracked-but-visible, which is why drift is at least countable
durability.answer: NO DURABILITY. 1406 untracked watch/inbox files exist on exactly one disk, in no commit, with no off-host remote, and a same-disk backup 538 commits stale. Single point of failure = the physical disk.

concurrency.atomic_publish_detail: writeIndex() L529: writeFileSync(INDEX.json.tmp) then renameSync - atomic on same fs
concurrency.lost_update_risk: Two concurrent folds -> second renameSync publishes an index built from a stale base
concurrency.shared_temp_name_risk: Single fixed INDEX.json.tmp path shared by all writers; slow writer's bytes can be renamed by a fast one

self_documented_incident.quote: erased at 16:35:35Z by a concurrent stale-base whole-file write (the B2-250 disease, claimed for this file at 16:06:18Z by B2-280 whose snapshot predated the landing)
self_documented_incident.impact: a landed code block was erased 2 minutes after landing and had to be re-applied on moved bytes

torn_write_detection.torn_event_log_line: CAUGHT - B2-42 malformed-line gate, currently clean (3 malformed all grandfathered, 0 new of 3931 lines)
torn_write_detection.lost_update_valid_index_missing_items: NOT CAUGHT - index stays schema-valid, surviving items still hash correctly, no notion of 'registered then vanished from index'
torn_write_detection.consequence: validator can prove the index is internally broken but CANNOT prove it is complete - which is how the 9753-file omission grows unnoticed

false_positives.why: lane 0's own report describing an RSA key

secrets.caveat: 'no leak in the scanned text' - 7444 binaries (PDF/PNG/ZIP) and >8MB files were not scanned. The ENFORCEMENT gap stands regardless of today's bytes being safe.

dashboard/static/index.html.fallback: embedded evidence map via .catch(()=>{}) at L127

mag/api_gateway.py.note: has /room/inbox/{seat}, an unrelated per-seat room queue

consumers.split_brain: NOT a different copy - the board reads NO copy. The contract names /board/inbox as canonical and INDEX.json self-describes root/read_first/host_root as /board/inbox, but the board serves nothing at that path.

supported: validator exits 1 with 43 errors, growing to 45 in six minutes
index/disk drift is 1 dangling entry vs 9753 unindexed real files; validator sees 26
1406 untracked files under watch/inbox; watch/*.json does not match nested paths
only git remote is a same-disk directory, 538 commits stale, last fetched Sep 19
no index/event-log locking; tmp+rename atomic but read-modify-write is not; writer header records a stale-base write erasing landed code
board has zero inbox references; its only fetch 404s live
disputed: whether the 9753 unindexed files are meant to be indexed - qdrop_export(4979) and mrpool_export(2842) look like deliberate bulk exports and law 9 says the inbox is 'not a flattening operation', but nothing declares any directory out of scope, so the ENFORCEMENT gap is unarguable even if the CONTENT gap is partly intended
unproven: how long the gate has been red and whether anyone reads its exit code; no CI binding found, and whether the commit hook invokes it is not established
whether the 538-commit backup lag and 7-day-stale fetch are intentional batching or a silently broken push
whether the 38+ hash mismatches are in-flight appends that would clear on re-register, or genuine overwrites violating law 8 - not distinguishable without per-file mtime forensics
